tweets: A callee can regain control before a contract's first function call finishes, allowing repeated use of stale state.
This occurs when state updates happen after an external call rather than before it.
The standard remedy is to perform internal state changes prior to any external interaction.
Alternatively, developers may implement a reentrancy lock to block unwanted callbacks into the protected path.
A lock prevents control from returning to the caller while the callee is executing.
However, a lock does not stop the external callee from passing control back to the original contract.
